name: Apoorva Mehta
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Instacart in 2012 at age 26 and entered Y Combinator’s Summer 2012 batch, launching the on-demand grocery marketplace that later became a multi-billion-dollar public company.
early_history_summary: Born 1986 in Jodhpur, India; family moved to Libya then to Hamilton, Ontario when he was 14. Earned electrical engineering at University of Waterloo, worked briefly at BlackBerry/Qualcomm, then Amazon supply-chain engineering (2008). Left Amazon in 2010 for San Francisco, launched ~20 failed startups, then founded Instacart in 2012.
family_context_summary: Born in Jodhpur; father worked for an electric transmission-line company in Libya; immigrated to Canada at 14. Middle-class immigrant path; detailed wealth not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in electric transmission infrastructure; not a software/startup apprenticeship path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Amazon supply chain, Waterloo engineering, SF startup immersion, YC, immigrant persistence
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes/CNBC profiles agree Mehta was born 1986 and founded Instacart in 2012 at age 26, entering YC S12 after creative outreach. Prior Amazon supply-chain engineering and ~20 failed startups supplied domain reps; co-founders Max Mullen and Brandon Leonardo joined via YC. Family background is immigrant/middle-class with father’s infrastructure work, not tech capital. Later IPO wealth and Cloud Health Systems extend the trajectory.
starting_point: Born 1986 in Jodhpur, India; raised partly in Libya then Hamilton, Ontario after immigrating at 14; father worked in electric transmission; trained in electrical engineering at Waterloo.
current_position: Founder of Instacart (stepped down as CEO 2021, left entirely 2023 after IPO); founder/CEO of Cloud Health Systems; reported multi-hundred-million to ~$1B+ stake-related wealth at IPO exit period.

trajectory.event: Joined Amazon as a supply-chain engineer after short stints at BlackBerry and Qualcomm.
Left Amazon for San Francisco and began a string of ~20 failed startup experiments.
Founded Instacart and entered Y Combinator S12, launching grocery delivery via shopper marketplace.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 as Instacart scaled early grocery partnerships.
Became a billionaire on paper after pandemic-driven Instacart funding and growth.
Stepped down as Instacart CEO to executive chairman; later founded Cloud Health Systems.
Instacart IPO; Mehta exited the company with a large equity fortune.

name: Diane Powell Murray
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; documented path is Spelman BA 1974, Cornell MS 1976, TRW career from 1977, Candace Award 1982, and senior Northrop Grumman CIO/VP roles decades later—no verifiable material milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Graduated Spelman College (BA mathematics, 1974) and Cornell (MS operations research, 1976). Worked briefly at Eastman Kodak, then long career at TRW/Northrop Grumman in systems/software engineering and program management, rising to sector VP/CIO roles before retiring in 2009.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and secondary profiles document education and TRW/Northrop career awards (Candace 1982; Computerworld Premier 100 in 2006) but omit birth year. Without age-dated early breakout, age-26 eligibility cannot be established.

name: Fatma Özcan
category: Database systems researcher / principal software engineer
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; PhD completed 2001 at Maryland and IBM Almaden research career followed—major public awards (VLDB Women in Database Research 2022; ACM Fellow 2024) arrived decades later. No dated material milestone by age 26 verified.
early_history_summary: Undergraduate computer engineering at METU (Ankara); PhD University of Maryland, College Park (2001) on heterogeneous databases. Joined IBM Research Almaden, later pureXML/Db2 work, then principal software engineer at Google (from ~2020) on big-data infrastructure.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Google/IBM profiles document a strong industrial-research career but no birth year and no pre-26 dated breakout beyond ordinary graduate study.

name: Devin Coldewey
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found in reviewed sources; known as long-time TechCrunch writer/photographer (from ~2007) without a dated material founder/engineering milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Seattle-based tech writer and photographer; wrote for CrunchGear/TechCrunch network from 2007, later senior AI coverage; has also been associated with story roles outside pure product engineering.
evidence_summary: TechCrunch author bio and related profiles establish journalism career start around 2007 but provide no birth year or age-26 engineering/founding milestone suitable for this FE cohort bar.

name: David S. Miller
milestone_by_age_26: In 1996 at age 21–22, with Miguel de Icaza, ported the Linux kernel to Sun SPARC and presented the work at USENIX; by the late 1990s he was primary maintainer of the Linux IP networking layer while still under 26.
early_history_summary: Born November 26, 1974 in New Brunswick, New Jersey. Contributed to Linux kernel development from the mid-1990s while at Rutgers CAIP; co-ported Linux to SPARC (1996), became a core networking maintainer, worked at Cobalt Microserver, then joined Red Hat in 1999 where he has long been a top kernel gatekeeper.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond New Jersey birthplace.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Linux kernel mid-90s, SPARC port, netdev maintainer, open-source community, Rutgers CAIP
evidence_summary: Wikipedia (born 1974) and USENIX/Atlanta Linux Showcase records place the SPARC port and early networking maintainership in 1996–1998 when he was ~21–24. Second sources confirm multi-year kernel membership by 1998 and Red Hat employment from 1999. Family advantages undocumented; leverage is deep systems skill plus open-source network position during Linux’s rise.
starting_point: Born November 26, 1974 in New Brunswick, New Jersey; early path tied to Rutgers CAIP and volunteer Linux kernel development; family class not documented.
current_position: Long-time Red Hat kernel engineer; primary Linux networking subsystem maintainer and SPARC port maintainer; among top non-author signoff gatekeepers for many kernel cycles.

trajectory.event: Co-ported Linux to Sun SPARC with Miguel de Icaza while at Rutgers CAIP.
Presented SPARC Linux work at USENIX; contributed major networking performance patches (e.g., socket hashing).
Described as nearly 5-year kernel team member and primary IP networking layer maintainer while at Cobalt Networks.
Joined Red Hat as a kernel developer, beginning a multi-decade maintainer tenure.
Delivered a keynote at the Ottawa Linux Symposium.
Established as a top kernel gatekeeper (non-author signoffs) from the 2.6.22 era onward.
Keynoted netdev 0.1 on the state of Linux kernel networking.

name: Jeff Sutherland
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1941; West Point graduation 1964 (age ~23) and Vietnam service precede the defining Scrum work at Easel (1993) and OOPSLA formalization with Ken Schwaber (1995) at ages ~52–54. No material software/product milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: US Military Academy graduate (1964), fighter pilot in Vietnam, later Stanford MS statistics and academic/medical career before software executive roles. Co-created Scrum in the 1990s and remains associated with Scrum Inc.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Scrum Guide bios date birth to June 20, 1941 and place Scrum creation in mid-1990s—far past age 26. Early military/academic path is not the FE-relevant breakout.

name: Olaf Carlson-Wee
milestone_by_age_26: In 2013 at age ~24, after cold-emailing his Vassar Bitcoin thesis to Coinbase’s founders, he became Coinbase’s first employee, ran early support/risk, and was paid in bitcoin for three years.
early_history_summary: Born 1989 in Northfield, Minnesota; studied sociology at Vassar (class of 2012) with an undergraduate thesis on Bitcoin and open-source finance. Joined Coinbase as employee #1 in 2013; left in 2016 (age ~27) to found Polychain Capital, which scaled into a major crypto fund with A16Z/Sequoia/etc. LPs.
family_context_summary: Raised in Minnesota (Northfield/Moorhead area references); brothers Kai and Anders Carlson-Wee are poets. Detailed family wealth not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a finance/crypto family path; siblings are literary rather than financial-domain apprentices.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bitcoin thesis, Coinbase employee #1, crypto wave, Vassar, cold email
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, CNBC, and YC Employee #1 interviews agree on 1989 birth, 2012 Vassar graduation, and 2013 Coinbase hire as first employee at ~24—well before age 26. Polychain founding in 2016 is slightly over 26 but compounds the early Coinbase crypto immersion. Family finance advantages not documented.
starting_point: Born 1989 in Northfield, Minnesota; sociology student at Vassar who wrote an undergraduate thesis on Bitcoin; family literary rather than finance-domain background.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Polychain Capital, a major cryptocurrency investment firm; former Coinbase employee #1 and head of risk; Forbes 30 Under 30 (2018).

trajectory.event: Graduated Vassar with a sociology degree and Bitcoin/open-source finance thesis.
Became Coinbase’s first employee after cold-emailing founders; handled early support and later risk, paid in bitcoin.
Left Coinbase and founded Polychain Capital with early LP capital focused on blockchain tokens.
Appeared on Forbes cover amid crypto boom; Polychain AUM claimed near $1B.
Named Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance and Fortune 40 Under 40.
Polychain reported multi-billion AUM as Coinbase IPO and DeFi cycle elevated crypto funds.

name: James Allan (computer scientist)
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; MS/PhD Cornell (1991/1995) and UMass Amherst faculty career with ACM Fellow (2020) recognition arrive as standard academic milestones without a verified dated breakout by age 26.
early_history_summary: Studied mathematics at Grinnell; MS and PhD in computer science at Cornell (1991, 1995). Joined UMass Amherst CIIR community in the mid-1990s and became a leading IR researcher and later distinguished professor/administrator.
evidence_summary: UMass/CIIR and Wikipedia profiles establish IR academic career and 2020 ACM Fellowship but omit birth year and any exceptional pre-26 milestone beyond graduate study.

name: John H. Booske
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; PhD nuclear engineering/plasma physics path (~1980–1985) and long UW–Madison ECE professorship indicate a conventional academic timeline without a verified material milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: American electrical engineer specializing in high-power microwaves, vacuum electronics, and bioelectromagnetics; longtime professor (later emeritus) at University of Wisconsin–Madison with IEEE and related fellowships.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and UW directory establish senior academic career without birth year or age-dated early breakout suitable for age-26 eligibility.

name: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
category: Author / tech career founder (Cracking the Coding Interview)
milestone_by_age_26: In 2008 at age ~26 she self-published the first edition of Cracking the Coding Interview and built CareerCup into the defining interview-prep platform for big-tech software hiring.
early_history_summary: Born 1982; educated at Episcopal Academy and University of Pennsylvania (BSE and MSE computer science, 2005). Worked as a software engineer at Google (including hiring-committee experience), Apple, and Microsoft, and as VP engineering at a startup before founding CareerCup and publishing CTCI, later adding Wharton MBA and further Cracking books.
family_context_summary: Not richly documented in reviewed sources beyond elite prep-school/Penn path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Penn CS, Google/Apple/Microsoft SWE, hiring committee, CareerCup, CTCI
evidence_summary: Wikipedia/Library of Congress place birth in 1982; CTCI first edition is widely dated to 2008 (Goodreads Oct 14, 2008), i.e., age 25–26. Prior Google and peer big-tech engineering jobs supplied direct domain exposure for interview content. Family background largely undocumented; advantages center on elite education and insider hiring experience.
starting_point: Born 1982; trained at Episcopal Academy and University of Pennsylvania CS (BSE/MSE 2005); early path through elite US education into big-tech engineering roles.
current_position: Founder/CEO of CareerCup; bestselling author of Cracking the Coding Interview and related interview books; tech hiring consultant and speaker.

trajectory.event: Completed Penn BSE/MSE in computer science and entered software engineering roles at major tech firms including Google.
Self-published first edition of Cracking the Coding Interview and scaled CareerCup as interview-prep infrastructure.
Published Cracking the PM Interview with Jackie Bavaro, expanding the series beyond coding interviews.
Released the widely used 6th edition of Cracking the Coding Interview (189 questions).
Delivered University of Pennsylvania Engineering masters commencement address.
Published Beyond Cracking the Coding Interview, updating strategies for modern hiring and negotiation.

name: Guy Blelloch
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; Swarthmore BA 1983 and MIT PhD 1988 (Vector Models for Data-Parallel Computing) place the main academic breakout near typical late-20s PhD timing, not a verified ≤26 milestone.
early_history_summary: Graduated Swarthmore (BA Physics / BS Engineering, 1983), earned MIT PhD under Charles Leiserson (1988), joined CMU faculty in 1988, and became a leading figure in parallel algorithms (ACM Fellow, Kanellakis Award, etc.).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and IEEE/CMU profiles document Swarthmore 1983 → MIT PhD 1988 → CMU career without a confirmed birth year; cannot honestly claim a dated ≤26 material milestone.

name: Eric Meyer
category: Web standards / CSS advocate and author
milestone_by_age_26: CSV/secondary sources place birth around 1967; CWRU BA 1992 (~age 25) and early web work from 1993 are ordinary early career. Defining CSS1 test suite, WaSP CSS Samurai role, and books arrived ~1997–2000 (ages ~30–33). No material ≤26 milestone found.
early_history_summary: Graduated Case Western Reserve University in 1992 (history BA with AI/astronomy/English minors); served as CWRU hypermedia systems manager 1992–2000; became a leading CSS educator/advocate (CSS1 test suite 1998, books from 2000, Netscape stint 2001–2003).
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources for early life; later personal life includes family and memorial CSS color rebeccapurple.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia lacks birth year (batch CSV lists 1967); career milestones that made him the CSS reference figure (test suite 1998, books 2000+) fall after age 26 if born 1967. Pre-26 record is university study and early campus hypermedia job, not a field-defining milestone.
